review_body: State Coroner of South Australia (Coroner Schapel)
report_title: Annual Report of the State Coroner 2015-2016
recommendation_text: I recommend, as the State Coroner has recommended in the matter of the death of Mrs Zahra Abrahimzadeh, that all aspects of domestic violence policing be characterised by a sense of curiosity, questioning and listening. Risk assessment must be actually applied, not merely recited as a mantra.
_note: Coroner Schapel explicitly repeats Coroner Johns' Abrahimzadeh recommendation 1 verbatim in this separate case, citing it directly — a clean, coroner-acknowledged repeat.
source_quote: On 25 September 2015, SAPOL implemented amendments to General Order – Domestic Abuse which included 'a sense of curiosity' within the philosophies outlined in the General Order. The 'sense of curiosity' philosophy was included in the 'Policing Domestic Violence 2015' training that was delivered to all sworn members, Call Centre Operators and Client Services Operators.

review_body: State Coroner of South Australia (Coroner Schapel)
report_title: Annual Report of the State Coroner 2015-2016
recommendation_text: I further recommend that in cases such as these, which for the purposes of SAPOL General Orders may not necessarily be characterised as involving violence or potential violence of a domestic nature, that all complaints of a similar nature be referred to police officers who have training in domestic violence risk assessment. At the very least, all such complaints should immediately be drawn to the attention of an officer of the rank of Sergeant or above.
source_quote: All sworn SAPOL members are trained in the management of DV-related incidents and DV risk assessments. [...] any incident which is recognised as being DV-related is subject to oversight by the submitting member's line manager who is of or acting at the rank of Sergeant.

review_body: State Coroner of South Australia (Coroner Schapel)
report_title: Annual Report of the State Coroner 2015-2016
recommendation_text: I further recommend that within SAPOL General Order Domestic Violence the definitions of 'Domestic partner' and 'Close personal relationship' be amended to encompass circumstances akin to those that existed between Ms Rankine and Mr Harding-Roots.
_note: Overtaken by legislative change that predates the report: the Intervention Orders (Prevention of Abuse) Act 2009 replaced the Domestic Violence Act 1994 in Dec 2011 and already broadened the relevant definitions before this recommendation was published.
source_quote: This recommendation is covered in the current General Order.

review_body: State Coroner of South Australia (Coroner Schapel)
report_title: Annual Report of the State Coroner 2015-2016
recommendation_text: I further recommend that police be directed to carefully consider whether in a complaint made in the context of a domestic situation involves the commission of a criminal offence. I further recommend that investigations into offences committed in that context be given priority.
source_quote: General Order Domestic Abuse outlines that DV/DA incidents are to be treated as a priority, including specific instructions in relation to management of DV incidents assessed as 'high risk'.
